correctness.rationale: Condition on one fixed gradient population g_i, persistent R of size r, fresh S uniformly without replacement from complementary M=N-r, with s>=1, B=r+s<N. Inclusion probabilities yield E||gbar_S-b||²=(M-s)V/[s(M-1)]. The two estimators are U=(1-q)a+q gbar_S and C=(1-p)a+p gbar_S, where q=s/B, p=M/N, D=p-q>0. Their bias and variance follow by shared centered noise, giving Var(C)/Var(U)=(p/q)² if V>0. For G_t=(1-t)U+tC, MSE=(1-t)²D²||a-b||²+(q+tD)² sigma². Differentiation yields the constrained oracle t*, with t*<1 for sigma²>0, and full-correction/no-correction threshold Delta²>(p+q)sigma²/D. The 50% overlap expression reduces to (2-B/N)². Independent exact-rational subset enumeration for five populations corroborated, but the unrestricted statement uses finite-population algebra.

originality.rationale: Lapucci–Pucci Section 5.1.1 analyzes the biased persistent estimator, proves a fully unbiased correction in Proposition 5.1, and reports its practical degradation in Remark 2. It does not compute the conditional variance inflation, shrinkage interpolation MSE, or oracle partial correction. Classical Horvitz–Thompson sampling yields ingredient inclusion probabilities, but not the source-specific optimized frontier as a finished mathematical statement. Generic shrinkage equivalence is a residual risk.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent two-estimator shrinkage formula could appear under generic survey-sampling terminology.
The optimal t* depends on inaccessible full-complement contrast and dispersion; no directly implementable adaptive method or convergence guarantee follows.
